t.7.90.1: Then, after some time had passed, Yudhājit, the Kekaya king, sent his own guru to the great-souled Rāghava.
t.7.90.3: The king gave to Rāma woollen blankets and jewels, an excellent garment of many colours, and many ornaments as well.
t.7.90.2: He sent Gārgya, the son of Aṅgiras, a brahmarṣi of boundless splendor, together with ten thousand horses as an unsurpassed gift of affection.
t.7.90.4: But Rāghava, having heard that the great seer Gārgya had arrived, come as the dear envoy of his maternal uncle Aśvapati,
t.7.90.5: Kākutstha, together with his followers, went out a full krośa to meet Gārgya, and having accepted that wealth, he honored him duly.
t.7.90.6: Having asked after all his welfare and that of his maternal uncle, Rāma began to question the illustrious, joy-bringing guest who was seated there.
t.7.90.7: What message has my maternal uncle sent, for the sake of which you, revered one, have come here, O best of those skilled in speech, like Bṛhaspati himself in person?
t.7.90.8: Having heard Rāma's words, the brahmarṣi began to relate to Rāghava the full account of the matter, which seemed wondrous.
t.7.90.9: O mighty-armed one, O bull among men, your maternal uncle Yudhājit has spoken words full of affection; let them be heard, if it pleases you.
t.7.90.10: This land of the Gandharvas, adorned with fruits and roots, lying on both sides of the Sindhu, is a most beautiful country.
t.7.90.11: And that land is guarded by the Gandharvas, armed and skilled in warfare, the heroic sons of Śailūṣa, three crores in number and of great strength.
t.7.90.12: Having conquered them, O Kākutstha, settle the fair land of the Gandharvas, O mighty-armed one, and with a well-composed mind found two cities there.
t.7.90.13: No one else can go there, and this region is exceedingly beautiful. Let it be pleasing to you, O mighty-armed one; I do not speak untruth to you.
t.7.90.14: Hearing that word of the great sage and of his maternal uncle, Rāghava was pleased; he said, "Very well," and looked toward Bharata.
t.7.90.15: Delighted, Rāghava, his hands joined in reverence, said to the twice-born one: "O brahmarṣi, these two princes will conquer that land."
t.7.90.16: The two heroic sons of Bharata, Takṣa and Puṣkala, were well protected by their maternal uncle, and both were steadfast in dharma.
t.7.90.17: Placing Bharata at their head, the two princes, accompanied by troops and followers, will slay the sons of the Gandharvas and divide the two cities between them.
t.7.90.18: Having founded those two excellent cities and settled his two sons in them, the exceedingly righteous one will come back to my side once more.
t.7.90.19: Having thus spoken to the brahmarṣi, he then gave his command to Bharata, who was accompanied by his army and followers, and had the two princes consecrated.
t.7.90.20: Under an auspicious constellation, placing the son of Aṅgiras at the head, Bharata set forth with his army and the two princes.
t.7.90.21: Then that army, as if accompanied by Śakra himself, marched forth from the city, followed a long way by Rāghava, invincible even to the suras and asuras.
t.7.90.22: Flesh-eating creatures and very huge Rākṣasas followed Bharata, out of thirst for blood.
t.7.90.23: And many hosts of beings, flesh-eaters exceedingly dreadful, came by the thousands, eager to devour the flesh of the sons of the Gandharvas.
t.7.90.24: Many thousands of lions, tigers and jackals, and of birds that range the sky, went on ahead of the army.
t.7.90.25: Having spent a month and a half on the road, the army, free from all affliction and thronged with cheerful, well-fed men, reached Kekaya.
